content: The CORONA trial aimed to evaluate the effects of administering 10 mg of rosuvastatin daily in patients diagnosed with congestive heart failure. This study was conducted as a double-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled trial. A total of 5011 patients with ischemic, systolic heart failure classified as New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class II, III, or IV were enrolled. These participants were randomly assigned to receive either 10 mg of rosuvastatin daily or a placebo. The primary outcomes assessed in the trial included death from cardiovascular causes, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and non-fatal stroke. The results demonstrated that rosuvastatin effectively reduced serum low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol levels while increasing high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol and triglyceride levels. Despite these favorable changes in lipid profiles, the use of rosuvastatin did not lead to a statistically significant reduction in mortality from cardiovascular causes, coronary events, or all-cause mortality.
